discussion.body:
`.stbsp` files contain helper data for texture streaming

Our biggest official resource on their creation & use is this GDC talk:
 * GDC on YouTube: [Efficient Texture Streaming in Titanfall 2](https://youtu.be/4BuvKotqpWo)
 
[`bsp_tool.extensions.stbsp.StreamBsp`](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/blob/master/bsp_tool/extensions/stbsp.py) maps the format

## How Respawn Generates `.stbsp`
As part of their internal commit & build systems at respawn, they used [Jenkins](https://www.jenkins.io/) to generate `.stbsp`

This work was dispatched to their "Precomputation Cruncher", pictured below:
![stbsp_gpu_cruncher](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/assets/36507175/71835f04-68fa-4e0e-80ba-3896a8dff71f)

From what I understand of the GDC talk, they would do a histogram of texture scale relative to a "probe"
Essentially a virtual player that looks at the map & decides what texture resolution looks best

`.stbsp` files seem to store the results of these histograms in some way, indexing specific material names
Mostly targetting `.rpak` materials, though some `.vmt` support exists

## Columns
![complex3_stbsp_deadzones3](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/assets/36507175/0967dad5-6085-49b6-ac2a-59a568809a69)
`.stbsp` contains columns (not unlike `CM_GRID`)
Each column is linked to some binary data we haven't reversed yet
@r-ex actually looked at the files in ida & figured out that what I thought was a histogram colour is instead `coverage_scale`
idk what that does specifically, so I'm visualising it as a colour

### Exporting
```python
>>> from bsp_tool.extensions.stbsp import StreamBsp
>>> StreamBsp.from_file(".../Titanfall2/r2/maps/mp_complex3.stbsp").columns_as_obj("complex3.obj")
```
### Colourising
> In Blender python terminal
```python
>>> for m in D.materials:
...     if len(m.name) == 8:
...         rgba = int(m.name, 16)
...         r = rgba >> 24
...         g = (rgba >> 16) & 0xFF
...         b = (rgba >> 8) & 0xFF
...         a = rgba & 0xFF
...         m.diffuse_color = [255 / x if x != 0 else 0 for x in (r, g, b, a)]
```
> NOTE: might need to delete / rename the default material before this works
at ~8mins in the GDC Youtube video, they define "coverage" as how much of a `256x256` screen a `4096x4096` texture fills

## Column Data
### Empty Columns
Since we use columns, there's loads of empty space
Empty columns have some bytes of column data, but all bytes are `0x00`
If a column is empty: `coverage_scale` is `1.1754943508222875e-38` (`00 00 80 00`)
`2177/3355` columns are empty in `mp_complex3`

## Column Data
### Empty Columns
Since we use columns, there's loads of empty space
Empty colums have 32 bytes of column data, all 32 bytes are `0x00`
If a column is empty: `coverage_scale` is `1.1754943508222875e-38` (`00 00 80 00`)
`2177/3355` columns are empty in `mp_complex3`

nodes.body:
rexx & royalblue found code references in ida
it's an array of pairs of shorts
1st short is `bin` (mip) & `MaterialInfo` index
2nd short is `coverage` (multiply by `column.coverage_scale`)

The arrays are preceded by a short count of pairs (+1 for some reason) & `0xFFFF`
not always at the start, sometime preceeded by nulls
remember, empty columns start with nulls too
